newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB defends Argus' BHP job.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB defends Argus' BHP job.

text.p: The National Australia Bank (NAB) on Thursday defended the appointment of its chief executive officer, Don Argus, to the board of Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP).

"If there was any conflict in the demands on his time between BHP and the National Bank, he's assured us...that the National Bank will come out on top. On balance, we have no hesitation as a board in supporting his joining the BHP board," NAB chairman William Irvine told the bank's annual meeting.
Irvine was responding to a shareholder who raised concerns that Argus would be distracted from his duties at NAB by the BHP position.
Irvine said the bank would benefit from the strategic and technical knowledge Argus would gain from his time with BHP.
Argus, who has been at the bank for 41 years, knew NAB's operation "backwards", Irvine said.
